title: Someone Finally Fixed Installing Apps on a Mac
gist: A free third-party utility called EasyDMG, built by developer Jeff Schumann, automates the 25-year-old macOS disk-image install ritual (mount, drag, unmount, delete) into a double-click. The piece is a light how-to, but it flags a persistent UX gap in Apple's non-App-Store software distribution path that Apple has left unaddressed since 2001.

insights.claim: Installing Mac software from outside the Mac App Store still requires the same multi-step disk-image ritual — download a DMG, mount a virtual disk, drag the app to Applications, unmount, delete the DMG — that Apple introduced with Mac OS X in 2001 and has not modernized in a quarter-century.
insights.speaker: Justin Pot
insights.so_what: A durable, unfixed friction point on the non-App-Store distribution path is a soft tax on every Mac ISV that avoids Apple's 15-30% store cut; watch whether regulatory pressure on sideloading pushes Apple to finally streamline it.
insights.quote: To be fair, it was relatively streamlined back in 2001 when it became the main way to install applications on the then-new Mac OS X. But that was a quarter-century ago, and there has to be a better way by now.
insights.locator: One of the oddest things about macOS

insights.claim: Independent developer Jeff Schumann shipped EasyDMG, a free macOS utility that registers itself as the default handler for DMG files and performs mounting, verification, installation, source-file cleanup and Finder reveal automatically.
insights.speaker: Justin Pot
insights.so_what: Illustrates how quickly indie developers close first-party UX gaps for free, capping the monetizable surface for any paid utility aimed at the same problem.
insights.quote: This completely free app has an adorable hamster mascot and the slogan “Created out of spite.”

insights.claim: EasyDMG ships with zero telemetry and makes only one network request — an update check — and does not run as a background process, launching only when a DMG is opened and quitting after install.
insights.speaker: Justin Pot
insights.so_what: No-telemetry, no-daemon design is now a marketable default in the indie Mac utility segment, raising the trust bar for commercial vendors whose analytics SDKs are increasingly a liability.
insights.quote: The application doesn't have any telemetry, either; the only network request it makes is checking for updates.
insights.locator: EasyDMG doesn't run in the background

insights.claim: The tool exposes a setting to disable all macOS warnings about apps from unidentified developers, a toggle the reviewer explicitly advises against using.
insights.speaker: Justin Pot
insights.so_what: Third-party install handlers that can switch off unsigned-developer warnings create a new malware-delivery vector on the Mac and are a plausible trigger for tighter Apple restrictions on default-handler registration.
insights.quote: You can disable all warnings about apps from unidentified developers (you probably shouldn't do this).

insights.claim: The bootstrap problem persists even for the fix: EasyDMG itself must be installed using the same manual DMG drag-and-drop process it is designed to eliminate.
insights.speaker: Justin Pot
insights.so_what: A reminder that user-space workarounds cannot fix distribution-layer friction at the point of first contact — only an OS-level change by Apple can.
insights.quote: simply download the application and install it using the very same installation dance you're trying to avoid
